anna: Quick sync: we need a final decision on fetch strategy for the JS SDK. Options we're weighing: always rely on globalThis.fetch, ship an optional undici fallback, or provide a small bundled server-only package. goal: minimal friction for edge + modern Node users, predictable behavior for older Node and serverless.

raul: lean towards "prefer global, dynamic undici fallback". keeps edge DX clean. but we must be explicit about packaging and dependency types so users don't hit "undici not found" at runtime.

li: packaging note: Recommend adding `undici` as an optionalDependency in our server build artifact and documenting adding it to projects that still run on Node <18. avoid peerDep because consumers forget to install. optionalDep means npm will try to install but won't fail installs for edge-only consumers.

mike: +1. also add an `exports` conditional entry in package.json so bundlers targeting edge/runtime pick the ESM edge-friendly entry. example: 
```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
  "node": { "default": "./dist/node/index.js" },
  "browser": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
}
```
This avoids landing undici in edge bundles.

anna: nice. TypeScript issues: users on Node that rely on undici complain about missing dom types (Request/Response). thoughts?

li: we should publish a tiny `types/fetch-shims.d.ts` and recommend `typeRoots` OR using `npm i -D @types/node-fetch` is fragile. simpler: `/// <reference lib="dom" />` in our SDK entry types or instruct TS config to include "DOM" in libs. also include a `types` entry in package.json pointing to our shim.

raul: runtime helper idea: `getSdkFetch({preferEnv, force})` that checks: 
1) if env var SDK_FETCH=undici -> load undici
2) else if typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function' -> return globalThis.fetch
3) else -> dynamic import('undici') and return u.fetch
Add a small wrapper `wrapFetch(fetch, {auth, retry})` so auth/retry logic is applied uniformly.

mike: streaming differences: undici's fetch response.body is a web stream in modern versions but earlier versions used Node streams. we should pin a compatible undici version and write unit tests that run on Node 18, Node 20, Deno, and Vercel edge to validate streaming behavior for large responses.

ci-bot: test-runner kicked off: fetch-adapter-matrix (node18,node20,deno,bun,vercel) :rocket:

li: bundlers to call out in docs: Vite/Rollup/Turbopack/Next SWC. note: when apps use tree shaking and conditional exports, ensure their bundler resolves our edge entry for edge builds. provide Next.js example for app/edge vs pages/api.

anna: docs snippet for troubleshooting: 
- Error: "Cannot find module 'undici'": add `npm i undici` on server-side or use our server bundle.
- "TS2339: Property 'body' does not exist on type Response": ensure `--lib DOM` or add our types shim.
- "Bundle includes undici in edge lambda": check package.json exports/conditional and ensure `browser`/`edge` fields point to no-undici entry.

raul: CI determinism: add SDK_FETCH env override and a test matrix flag to force each code path (global vs undici) so snapshots don't flake based on hosted runner Node version.

mike: I'll open PRs: 1) runtime helper + env override, 2) package.json export adjustments + optionalDependency change, 3) types shim + docs. li will add integration tests for streaming and edge.

anna: perfect. file a ticket and link PRs. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
